subject: Post-call: measurement windows, streaming behavior, and proposed remedy language
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@upscale.ai>, Timothy Brown <tim@upscale.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@gmail.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: measurement windows, streaming behavior, and proposed remedy language

Hi Elena / Tim —

Thanks again for the call earlier — helpful to hear more about the real-time search use case and the SLA expectations from your ops team. Per request, I wanted to summarize the measurement points we discussed and capture a few open questions so we can draft formal SLA language.

Summary of what we heard from Upscale AI:
- P95 latency target for single-turn generation: 120ms (for 256 token prompt, model X-7b-qs)
- Concurrent inference: expected bursts to 400 concurrent streams during peak windows (10–12 PST)
- Streaming requirement: audio transcription + token streaming to UI with <200ms first-byte for live UX
- Reporting cadence: weekly incident report + monthly SLO dashboard export to your retention bucket

Open / clarifying items we flagged on the call:
1) Measurement window: do you want rolling 5-minute windows for concurrency/throughput accounting, or per-request averaged baselines?
2) Exclusions: planned maintenance windows, customer-caused network issues, and upstream model failovers — which should be carved out?
3) Remedy preference: crediting model-token usage vs. service credit (monthly invoice offset) — which is simpler for your finance team?

Next steps I propose:
- We (Redwood) send a short draft of the SLO language that defines measurement method (sampling/aggregation), exclusions, and a tiered remedy matrix.
- Engineering confirms streaming first-byte measurement technique (server-to-client vs. end-to-end browser measurement).
- HubSpot deal note updated with agreed measurement window and remedy type by EOD Monday.

I've attached the recording and will drop a short SLO-draft this afternoon for your review. Marcus — looping you for legal/ops wording; Lauren — can you confirm typical remedy language we use for mid-market deals?

Thanks,

— Priyom
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Post-call: measurement windows, streaming behavior, and proposed remedy language

Thanks Priyom — great recap. A few quick clarifications from our side so your SRE/legal teams can draft accurately: 

1) Measurement window: prefer rolling 5-minute windows for concurrent stream counts and a 24-hour rolling window for availability. For latency SLOs (P95), use a 1-hour aggregated sampling to avoid microburst noise.
2) Exclusions: planned maintenance (>= 30 minutes with notice), customer-origin network outages (we will provide traceroute + CDN logs), and model-level degradations where Redwood triggers an automatic fallback to a lower-fidelity variant. We do want visibility into model fallbacks and for them to count separately (i.e., not throw to the overall SLO failure unless fallback also exceeds latency threshold).
3) Streaming measurement: critical for our UX — we prefer server-to-client first-byte at the Redwood edge as the canonical metric (we can augment with client-side SDK telemetry later).
4) Remedies: service credit applied as percentage of monthly invoice is easiest for procurement; token credit is messy for our billing reconciliation.

Finally, for concurrency: our ops expects graceful degradation beyond 400 concurrent streams (queueing up to 100 more, with explicit 503 if we hit hard cap). Does Redwood support configurable queueing policies per customer?

If you can incorporate the above into the draft SLA language that would be perfect. Happy to jump on a quick follow-up call if useful.

Best,
Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Ops, Upscale AI
elena@upscale.ai

Hi Elena / Tim —

Thanks for the clear directions — we can definitely incorporate these into contractual language. Below is a concise draft we can iterate on; I've attached a PDF with expanded wording and examples.

DRAFT SLA SNIPPET (proposal) — to be inserted into Section 2.2 (Performance Objectives):

1) Latency Measurement:
- Latency SLOs (e.g., P95 <= 120ms) shall be measured at the Redwood edge using server-to-client first-byte timing for generation requests. Observations shall be aggregated into 1-hour sampling windows for the purposes of P95 calculation; a minimum of 1,000 samples per 1-hour window is required for the window to be valid.

2) Concurrency and Throughput:
- Concurrency counts shall be computed using rolling 5-minute windows. Concurrent streams exceeding the committed capacity shall be subject to Redwood's customer-level queueing policy; Redwood will support a configurable soft-queue of up to 25% above committed concurrency with a hard cap that returns 503 responses.

3) Exclusions:
- Agreed exclusions include planned maintenance (>= 30 minutes with 48 hours' notice), customer-origin network outages (where the customer provides packet captures/traceroutes), and model-variant automatic fallbacks. Automatic fallbacks shall be logged and surfaced to customer telemetry; they will not count as SLO failures unless the active variant also violates the latency threshold.

4) Reporting and Remedies:
- Redwood will publish weekly incident summaries and a monthly SLO export to the customer's designated storage location.
- Remedies for missed SLOs shall be a service credit equal to a percentage of the monthly invoice calculated on the proportion of invalidated windows, with a caps schedule detailed in Appendix A (see attached PDF). Token credits are available only by mutual agreement and require separate billing reconciliation.

If that aligns with you, I'll have legal convert this into contractual language and include the Appendix A table for remedy percentages. Next practical step: confirm the minimum samples requirement and whether Upscale wants a distinct logging webhook for automatic fallback events.

Open to a 30-minute follow-up Monday to sign off.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
